transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood CSM); Carla (PM, StellarCare), Mark (Head of AI), Jenna (Security), Tom (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align onboarding timeline for StellarCare's pilot with Redwood Dedicated and confirm security/compliance checks and performance baseline.

Topics:
- Onboarding timeline and milestones
- Network / VPC / private deployment questions
- Security: SOC2, audit logs, KMS/HSM
- Performance baseline and benchmarking plan
- Next steps and action items

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick intros?
[00:20] Carla: Hi all, Carla here, Product at StellarCare. excited to get started.
[00:27] Priya: Hi, Priya SE, i'll lead the technical onboarding and the baseline perf tests.
[00:33] Mark: Mark Liu, head of AI. main goal is to get consistent latency under 200ms for our critical endpoints.
[00:43] Jenna: Jenna, security. i want to cover encryption, audit logs, and data residency right away.
[00:49] Tom: Tom, DevOps, i'll handle network / infra details.
[00:54] Daniel: Daniel, Customer Success, i'll coordinate milestones and make sure we hit the pilot dates.

[02:05] Alex: Great. high level we propose a 6-week onboarding: week 1 infra + access, week 2 model pinning and configs, week 3 perf baselines, week 4 pilot, week 5 rollouts and week 6 handoff. flexible though.
[02:45] Carla: That sounds good; our timeline is fairly aggressive — we want pilot traffic in 5 weeks if possible.
[03:10] Priya: We can compress some tasks. the infra prep is key: VPC peering, route tables, firewall rules. Tom, what's your current cloud setup?
[03:26] Tom: We're on GCP, primarily GKE, and running a small ML infra in a separate project. we'll need a VPC peering option or private endpoints.
[03:40] Priya: Redwood Private supports V-P-C peering and a private control plane; we also have on-prem packages if needed but for GCP peering should be straightforward. note, sometimes the auto docs call it Redwood 'Private Plane' — small doc typo.
[04:05] Jenna: For security we need SOC 2 type II, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integration. also audit logs retention for 7 years ideally.
[04:22] Alex: We are SOC 2 compliant, SSO via SAML supported, RBAC in the console, and KMS/HSM integrations are available — i'll attach the security pack after the call.
[04:51] Mark: One question on logs: can we ship token-level usage logs into our SIEM?
[05:10] Priya: Yes, we have options: streaming audit logs to customer S3 or BigQuery, and we can integrate with SIEM. slight caveat — PII redaction for logs is configurable.
[05:37] Jenna: Good; for compliance we need proof of encryption at rest and in transit and key ownership; we prefer customer-managed keys.
[05:50] Alex: Customer-managed keys supported via KMS. we'll note that in the runbook.

[07:05] Priya: On the inference side, we should talk about model variants. are you planning to use open models or private model uploads?
[07:20] Mark: We'll start with an open Llama-3 style family and then move to a tuned variant. mostly Gen2-style prompts for triage.
[07:33] Priya: Great. our runtime supports quantized variants and config suggestions. for lower latency we'd recommend a quantized 8-bit path, and we can benchmark both hosted and Dedicated.
[07:50] Tom: On Dedicated, what are the network egress patterns? we need to know if traffic leaves our VPC.
[07:58] Priya: For Dedicated with VPC, traffic stays inside customer network, no egress to public net. if you use hosted API it's different. some customers hybridize for cost.
[08:20] Carla: Cost is a concern. can we see an estimate for token costs vs Dedicated commit?
[08:32] Alex: yes i'll send the commit vs on-demand spreadsheets. generally Dedicated gives predictable throughput and unit cost reductions for steady traffic.

[09:45] Mark: Perf baseline: we'd like a realistic test harness and to measure p50/p95 latency at our prompt sizes. can the SE run a baseline with our prompts?
[09:58] Priya: absolutely. plan: 1) we get prompts, 2) SE provisions a baseline environment (can be a small Dedicated pool or hosted sim), 3) run ramp tests and measure latency/throughput and KV cache effects.
[10:30] Tom: what's KV cache? i've seen references but not implemented in our stack.
[10:36] Priya: KV cache — the key-value cache for autoregressive decoding; it preserves prefix states to reduce recompute on repeated context. can cut tokens and latency for chat-style flows. sometimes transcribed as "K V cache" or even "K-V cash" in our docs, so apologies for the typo.

[12:00] Jenna: On data residency — we need all data in us-east1 to meet internal regs. do you have regions there?
[12:08] Alex: yes, we support deployments in us-east1 and eu-west1 for our hosted tier. Dedicated can be deployed in the same region via our cloud partners. we'll note region options in the infra checklist.

[13:20] Carla: Integration points: our product needs both generation endpoints for triage and embeddings for semantic search.
[13:30] Priya: We recommend separate routes: one tuned for embeddings and one for generation with different batching/latency profiles. Redwood Console will show per-route token cost so you can attribute costs.
[13:55] Mark: How about model version pinning during rollouts? we need canary and automatic fallback for production.
[14:05] Alex: Rollouts supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous model variant on regression. we'll include a runbook snippet.

[15:20] Tom: On the network side, do you support private peering with shared VPCs?
[15:29] Priya: Yes, shared VPC peering is supported, but we need a few firewall ports open for the control plane; i'll include exact port list.

[17:00] Jenna: One more: audit logs format and schema — can we get a sample log schema?
[17:12] Priya: yes, i'll attach a sample with the runbook. note that some fields may have vendor-specific names, and the transcription sometimes has names like "audit-log" vs "audit_event" in docs.

[20:00] Alex: Let's talk timeline. if Priya sends the runbook by Friday, Tom provides network details next week, we can plan the perf baseline the week of 3/15. pilot traffic by 3/30 maybe. sound realistic?
[20:20] Carla: sounds good but we want pilot earlier if possible — we'll push to 3/25.
[20:28] Daniel: we'll explore compressing week 2 and 3 activities. SE to propose a condensed schedule.

[22:45] Priya: For the baseline we'll need a small test harness — JMeter or a simple node-based runner. i can provide a script and dashboard links.
[23:05] Mark: Also can we do a quick perf deep dive with kernel selection — we heard Redwood's runtime picks optimized kernels depending on seq length; can that be part of the SE session?
[23:20] Priya: yes, we'll include kernel selection, batching strategies, and quantization tradeoffs. sometimes our docs say "kernel selector" as a module name, but internally it's the compilation + kernel matcher.

[26:00] Carla: Security — will you provide a standard attestation or SOC 2 report?
[26:10] Alex: yes, we can provide SOC 2 report under NDA, and Jenna we can set up an audit packet share link after the call.

[28:00] Tom: For Dedicated capacity, what's the minimum commit? and how does autoscaling burst work?
[28:12] Alex: Dedicated minimum depends on region but typically a 4-GPU pool as a starter; autoscaling allows bursts and you can set policies. i'll include the Dedicated playbook which has numbers.

[30:40] Mark: On costs for batching — we want to avoid latency regressions per user. what are the knobs?
[30:50] Priya: knobs are max batch size, preferred latency SLO, and adaptive batching windows. Redwood Optimize can suggest initial settings based on workload. but there is always a tradeoff: higher batch size reduces unit cost but increases tail latency.

[33:10] Carla: Any blockers we foresee?
[33:20] Daniel: main blockers: network provisioning, security paperwork (NDA + SOC2 exchange), and prompt set availability from Mark's team.

[35:00] Alex: Ok let's recap real quick — items and owners: Priya runbook, Tom infra, Mark prompt sets, Alex pricing. also we agreed on a perf baseline week — we'll lock calendar after runbook is sent.

[36:45] Jenna: One more quick thing — do you support BYOK key rotation schedules?
[36:55] Priya: yes, key rotation supported; details in KMS integration doc. sometimes the doc examples use AWS KMS but we support GCP KMS too.

[39:00] Tom: i'll get the VPC diagrams over and a contact for our network team.

[42:10] Priya: i'll share links: onboarding runbook (link: drive.redwood.com/onboard/stellercare-runbook), security pack (link: drive.redwood.com/sec-pack), and a perf script (link: github.com/redwood/perf-harness). note: some links in the recording are auto-transcribed incorrectly.

[44:30] Carla: Thanks, appreciate the clarity. we'll aim to have network details and prompt sets by next Tuesday.

[45:10] Alex: Great. final ask — Alex will send pricing and Dedicated options; Priya will send runbook by Friday; schedule perf baseline for week of 3/15.

[47:50] Daniel: i'll create a follow-up calendar invite for the baseline workshop and include owners.

[49:00] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with the runbook and next milestones.

[49:10] Carla: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
